title: Novo Nordisk semaglutide proteomic aging-clock preprint: who was measured, and how many of 21 clocks moved
source: Dermit M, et al. Semaglutide reduces proteomic organ-specific biological age across randomized clinical trials. Research Square preprint, posted September 22, 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11082091/v1 (main text Table 1, Fig. 2b, Supplementary Fig. 2b; online methods).
transcribed_by: Jabbit, October 19, 2026 (~10 AM ET). Counts are the numbers printed on the bars of Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 2b (Holm-Bonferroni correction); not re-derived.
clocks: 18 organ clocks (adipose, adrenal, artery, brain, esophagus, heart, immune, intestine, kidney, liver, lung, muscle, pancreas, pituitary, salivary, skin, stomach, thyroid) + 3 composites (multiorgan, conventional, organismal), from Goeminne et al. 2025, Cell Metab (UK Biobank, mortality-trained)

SELECT.note: nested case-control subset: 781 of 1,641 had a MACE event vs 1,270 of 17,604 in the full trial
